scientific_queries.note: Decisive decomposition: does the annotation increment come from pathway or from tissue?

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round executes the decisive test it promised in R119 and overturns its own main positive claim.

what_this_overturns.the_claim: C74 and C80 attributed the increment to pathway annotation
what_this_overturns.the_decomposition: pathway is significant in 0 of 3 primary pools and negative in 2 of them, while tissue is significant in 2 of 3
what_this_overturns.so: what helps beyond drug identity is the cell's tissue, a three-level metadata field, which outperforms a thirty-eight-level pathway block
what_this_overturns.consequence: the programme's only positive modelling claim shrinks from 'annotation carries complementary information' to 'tissue carries information', which is close to a known confounder

the_unresolved_contradiction.consequence: no claim that pathway is entirely useless may be written until this is resolved

the_fourth_attribution_error.R99: attributed the increment to annotation when it was granularity
the_fourth_attribution_error.R102: attributed the baseline's edge to marginals when it was lack of shrinkage
the_fourth_attribution_error.R119: the increment reversed under tissue holdout
the_fourth_attribution_error.common_fix: remove one factor at a time

limits: pathway has 38 levels and tissue 3, so tissue may simply be better estimated rather than more informative
the three pools share one training set
the two criteria contradict each other on pathway
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: resolve the primary-versus-secondary contradiction on pathway before writing that pathway is useless

register_updates.C91: new and decisive: the increment is tissue, not pathway
